messages:
marta: Heads upI hit an annoying macOS combo: Homebrew-installed redwoodctl autoupdate fails, zsh completion doesn't load, and my profiles got duplicated during the installer migration. Anyone seen this stack before?

kevin: ouch. which brew package did you use (core/cask)? and what macOS version?

marta: homebrew core, redwoodctl 1.0.0, macOS 13.6.2. Install log shows a post-install auto-update step failing due to permission denied writing to /usr/local/Cellar/redwoodctl/... and then the installer re-ran the profile migration creating profile-name and profile-name-1. Also zsh completion tries to write to /usr/local/share/zsh/site-functions and fails.

lee: can you paste the exact errors?

marta: pasted trimmed output:
```
$ brew install redwoodctl
==> Installing redwoodctl v1.0.0
==> Running post-install hooks
/usr/local/bin/redwoodctl update-self --background
Error: permission denied while writing /usr/local/Cellar/redwoodctl/1.0.0/_update/state.json: open /usr/local/Cellar/redwoodctl/1.0.0/_update/state.json: permission denied
Warning: completion install failed: mkdir /usr/local/share/zsh/site-functions: permission denied
Migrating old profiles from ~/.redwood to ~/.config/redwood
wrote ~/.config/redwood/profiles.json
wrote ~/.config/redwood/profiles.json (profile-name-1)
```

marta: after that redwoodctl login opens the browser but then loops prompting for keychain access and eventually times out.

kevin: two things: 1) Homebrew on Intel macs expects /usr/local owner to be user, otherwise brew will warn. 2) keychain prompts during headless auth happen if the binary requests keychain but installer had to fallback and didn't set permissions.

lee: try `brew doctor` and `brew postinstall redwoodctl` to see more. Also `ls -ld /usr/local /usr/local/share/zsh/site-functions /usr/local/Cellar/redwoodctl` to check perms.

marta: tried those, output below:
```
$ ls -ld /usr/local/Cellar/redwoodctl
drwxr-xr-x  3 root  admin  96 Mar  5 10:22 /usr/local/Cellar/redwoodctl
$ ls -ld /usr/local/share/zsh/site-functions
drwxr-xr-x  3 root  admin  96 Mar  1 08:10 /usr/local/share/zsh/site-functions
```
so brew installed as root (packagemanager), but my user can't write.

diana: the quick fix is to `sudo chown -R $(whoami):admin /usr/local/Cellar/redwoodctl /usr/local/share/zsh/site-functions` then run `redwoodctl completion zsh > /usr/local/share/zsh/site-functions/_redwoodctl` or use `redwoodctl completion zsh | sudo tee /usr/local/share/zsh/site-functions/_redwoodctl`. For the profiles duplication: manual merge of ~/.config/redwood/profiles.json and remove the -1 entry.

kevin: we should be careful recommending chown on /usr/local broadly; suggest only on the specific redwoodctl paths. Also we can document a non-root install path: `brew install --prefix=$HOME/.homebrew redwoodctl` or use the tarball.

marta: after chown the autoupdate ran, completion installed, and login worked once I allowed keychain access. But curious about the profile duplication: why did migration run twice?

lee: likely the postinstall hook retried on failure and didn't mark the migration as complete because the write failed mid-flight, so second attempt added a new profile entry with suffix. We should add an atomic write + temp file rename in the migration to avoid partial writes.

ops-bot: Created issue #629: "installer(mac): handle permission errors during postinstall, avoid duplicate profile migration, and improve zsh completion install docs" 1https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwoodctl/issues/629

marta: filing repro notes and the ls outputs in the issue. TL;DR for others: if you see permission denied during brew postinstall, chown the specific redwoodctl directories, re-run postinstall, then check ~/.config/redwood/profiles.json for duplicates. Also `redwoodctl login --no-keychain` will skip keychain storage if you don't want macOS prompts.

diana: added a small docs blurb to onboarding: prefer non-root brew installs or use standalone installer on macs managed by IT, and `--no-keychain` hint.

marta: thanks all 38944d fixed my localdev flow. Closing thread.
